questions.question: Which two CSS properties are hardware-accelerated by the GPU, ensuring smooth 60fps animations?
questions.hint: Transform and opacity bypass layout and paint reflows.
questions.explanation: transform and opacity can be composited directly by the GPU, avoiding CPU layout (reflow) and repaint bottlenecks.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a transition and an @keyframes animation?
options: Transitions require a state change (like :hover) to run between two values, while @keyframes animations can run autonomously with multi-stage steps
questions.hint: Two-state transition vs multi-stage autonomous keyframes.
questions.explanation: A transition interpolates between two states when triggered; an @keyframes animation can run automatically with multiple intermediate stages.

questions.question: Why is transition: all considered a performance anti-pattern?
options: It forces the browser to monitor and interpolate every single CSS property, causing layout thrashing and jank
questions.hint: Animating every property causes unnecessary work.
questions.explanation: transition: all forces browser overhead on every property change; specifying explicit properties (e.g. transform, opacity) is much faster.

questions.question: Which animation property ensures the element retains the styles of the 100% final keyframe after completion?
questions.explanation: animation-fill-mode: forwards retains the styling applied by the last executed keyframe.

questions.question: Which timing function provides a constant, uniform speed throughout the animation from start to finish?
questions.explanation: linear progresses at an unvarying, constant speed, making it ideal for rotating spinners and clocks.
